row.response_b:
Pallas cats are rare and beautiful, specialized cat predators at home in the snowy, mountainous regions of Central Asia. They have long slender bodies and unusually long legs and large feet. Pallas cats hunt small to medium-sized prey such as marmot, hare, Granatic marmots, and small birds, and though graceful in movement, they are very agile and swift. Pallas cats have thick silvery-gray fur in winter, pale grayish-blue fur in summer months, and black spots on the coat. Pallas cats are genetically very similar to the smaller, more widespread Siberian cat (Leopardus sibiricus), and hybrids have been produced. Both cats are listed as Vulnerable by the IUCN and now dangerously close to extinction. Pallas cats have been hunted extensively over the centuries for their beautiful fur, and also due to their presence in agriculture as poultry predators.  Consequently, Pallas cats are listed by CITES as a species threatened with extinction and protected by Iran, Mongolia, Russia and South Korea.
